privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This policy describes the personal data processed by Registry, the purposes pursued, the retention periods and your rights, in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR).

controller.title: Data controller
controller.text: Registry involves two distinct processing activities. For the account data of the people who use the application, the data controller is Luc Aucoin. For the data of participants recorded in the registers, the data controller is the project organiser who records them, the publisher acting solely as a processor: see the "Participant data" section below.

participants.title: Participant data
participants.intro: A register holds data about people who do not use the application and have no account on it: participants. That data is entered by the project organiser. Registry processes the following on their behalf:
participants.identity: Identity: last name, first name, date of birth, and the resulting minor or adult status.
participants.presence: Presence: timestamped entries and exits, their reasons, and the groups and activities they are attached to.
participants.vehicles: Vehicles, where associated: licence plate, make and model.
participants.communications: Communications: free-text messages written by the organiser and attached to a movement.

roles.title: Roles and responsibilities
roles.organiser: The organiser who creates a project and records participants in it determines the purposes and means of that processing: they are the controller within the meaning of article 4(7) GDPR.
roles.publisher: The publisher of Registry acts as a processor within the meaning of article 28 GDPR: it processes that data only to provide the service, on the organiser's instructions, uses it for no other purpose, discloses it to no third party, and applies the security measures described in this policy. The hosting provider named in the legal notice is the only sub-processor.

consent.title: Informing participants and obtaining their consent
consent.text: It is the organiser's responsibility, not the publisher's, to have a lawful basis for recording a participant, to inform that participant of the processing, and to obtain their prior consent where consent is the lawful basis relied upon. By creating a project and entering participants into it, the organiser declares that they have met these obligations.
consent.noVerification: The publisher has no contact with participants and is not in a position to verify that this information was given or that this consent was obtained.
consent.minors: Where the participant is a minor, consent must be obtained from the holder of parental authority, in accordance with article 8 GDPR and article 45 of the French Data Protection Act, which sets that threshold at 15 years of age in France.

rights.title: How participants exercise their rights
rights.text: A participant wishing to exercise their rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction or objection must contact the organiser of the project that recorded them, who is the sole controller of that processing. A request sent to the publisher will be directed to that organiser, as the publisher is not entitled to answer it itself.

data.title: Data collected
data.intro: For the people who use the application, Registry only processes the data needed for it to work (participant data is covered in the previous section):
data.identity: Account data: name, email address, date of birth.
data.usage: Usage data: last-login date and audit identifiers (created by, modified by) attached to records.
data.telemetry: Technical telemetry, for signed-in users only: performance indicators (Core Web Vitals) and JavaScript errors, associated with the page path only — never with URL parameters or entered data. The IP address is used transiently for rate limiting and is not stored.

purposes.title: Purposes and legal bases
purposes.intro: Each processing activity relies on a legal basis from article 6 of the GDPR:
purposes.service: Providing the service (account, authentication, registry management) — performance of a contract (art. 6.1.b).
purposes.security: Securing the application (sessions, rate limiting, audit trail) — legitimate interest (art. 6.1.f).
purposes.telemetry: Measuring technical performance and detecting errors — legitimate interest (art. 6.1.f).
purposes.preferences: Remembering your display preferences (theme, language) — stored only at your explicit request.

retention.title: Retention periods
retention.text: User accounts and project data are automatically purged after 12 months of inactivity. Participant data is kept for the lifetime of the project it belongs to and is deleted with it; it is for the organiser to keep it only as long as their own purpose requires and to delete the project once that purpose is met. Cookies have the lifetimes listed in the table below.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.intro: You have the following rights over your personal data:
rights.access: right of access to your data;
rights.erasure: right to erasure: you can have your account anonymised directly from the "My account" page;
rights.portability: right to data portability: no automated export is available yet, please send your request by email;
rights.exercise: To exercise these rights, write to:
rights.complaint: You may also lodge a complaint with the CNIL (the French data protection authority):

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.intro: Registry uses no third-party cookies, no advertising trackers and no external audience-measurement tool.
cookies.noBanner: No consent banner is required: only cookies strictly necessary for the service are used, plus functional cookies set only after an explicit action on your part (choosing a theme or language) — all exempt from consent under the CNIL guidelines.

accessibilityPage.title: Accessibility statement
accessibilityPage.intro: Registry is committed to making its application accessible. The target standard is WCAG 2.2 (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines) level AA.

status.title: Conformance status
status.text: Registry is partially compliant with WCAG 2.2 level AA. Every non-conformity identified so far has been fixed, including those originating in third-party components, and the automated tests now run with no rule disabled. Full conformance will only be declared once the manual audit described below has been carried out.

exceptions.title: Known limitations
exceptions.manualAudit: the manual keyboard and screen-reader audit (NVDA, VoiceOver) of the critical journeys is still outstanding: automated tests cover only part of the criteria, so this audit is what full conformance depends on;
exceptions.thirdParty: third-party components (Ant Design Vue) are corrected by a patch maintained in the repository; a regression reintroduced by an upgrade would be caught by the automated tests before release.

testing.title: Preparation of this statement
testing.text: This statement was prepared on 4 August 2026. It relies on automated tests (axe-core) run continuously across the full WCAG 2.2 A and AA rule set, with no waivers, blocking any serious or critical regression.
